questions.question: How do you handle errors in RxJS? (catchError, retry, retryWhen)
questions.title: RxJS Error Handling — catchError, retry, retryWhen Examples
questions.direct_answer:
How do you handle errors in RxJS? (catchError, retry, retryWhen)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** catchError returns a replacement Observable; retry re-subscribes on error; retryWhen for custom retry (exponential backoff).

**Classic weak answer:** Placing catchError after a subscribe instead of inside the pipe — error handling must be inside the pipe to be part of the Observable.

**Senior finish:** Show an exponential-backoff retry pattern with retry({count, delay: error => timer(...)}); mention operator changes in RxJS 7+.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **RxJS Error Handling — catchError, retry, retryWhen Examples** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How do you handle errors in RxJS? (catchError, retry, retryWhen)

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **catchError returns a replacement Observable; retry re-subscribes on error; retryWhen for custom retry (exponential backoff)**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Placing catchError after a subscribe instead of inside the pipe — error handling must be inside the pipe to be part of the Observable**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show an exponential-backoff retry pattern with retry({count, delay: error => timer(...)}); mention operator changes in RxJS 7+**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** catchError returns a replacement Observable; retry re-subscribes on error; retryWhen for custom retry (exponential backoff)
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **placing catchError after a subscribe instead of inside the pipe — error handling must be inside the pipe to be part of the Observable** and what you do instead.

sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** catchError returns a replacement Observable; retry re-subscribes on error; retryWhen for custom retry (exponential backoff)
- **Pitfall:** Placing catchError after a subscribe instead of inside the pipe — error handling must be inside the pipe to be part of the Observable
- **Differentiator:** Show an exponential-backoff retry pattern with retry({count, delay: error => timer(...)}); mention operator changes in RxJS 7+
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **catchError returns a replacement Observable; retry re-subscribes on error; retryWhen for custom retry (exponential backoff)** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Placing catchError after a subscribe instead of inside the pipe — error handling must be inside the pipe to be part of the Observable** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Show an exponential-backoff retry pattern with retry({count, delay: error => timer(...)}); mention operator changes in RxJS 7+**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
